items.title: Accurate medical advice from AI can still be dangerous | STAT
items.summary: Some will argue that AI should be a neutral aggregator of information. But AI cannot be neutral: Every accurate answer excludes many additional facts and emphasizes some over others. Because of these choices, AI answers already influence behavior, as shown by the chickenpox party examples. [...] Artificial intelligence is delivering health guidance at an unprecedented scale. Every week, more than 300 million people ask ChatGPT health questions. Now, the federal government is moving AI deeper into medical care to communicate directly and autonomously with patients. Chris Klomp, the nominee for deputy secretary of Health and Human Services, has called AI in patient care the agency’s “holy grail” for improving the nation’s health. [...] Medical ethics pairs the duty to do no harm with beneficence, which is an affirmative obligation to do good. Safety evaluations of AI have focused mainly on the first duty by screening for responses that encourage imminent self-harm, discourage necessary care, or spread false information. Behavioral benchmarking would extend the first duty beyond imminent danger to long-term harms. It could also advance the second duty, which has received far less attention: designing AI to help people by

One theory about an AI Armageddon doesn't involve robots who look like Arnold Schwarzenegger hunting us down with laser guns. AI could just take over our natural habitat, as we've done with other animals and plants, which would leave us without food and shelter.

Here's a thought exercise: If AI were evaluating whether humans were worth saving for conservation purposes, would we grade out more as an invasive species or one that made important contributions to the ecosystem? [...] # Someone drained my bank account. Then the real nightmare began | Opinion

## Over time, AI is going to turn our brains to mush. People won't be able to remember phone numbers, basic grammar or directions to places they've visited once or twice without consulting AI overlords.

Portrait of Blake Fontenay

There's an old episode of "The Simpsons" where Homer, the TV show's booze-addled antihero, offers a hilarious toast: "To alcohol! The cause of – and solution to – all of life's problems." [...] People – some of us, at least – are worried about AI eventually overthrowing human civilization. Even more immediately, there's widespread concern about the proliferation of data centers needed to support AI operations.

Yet at the same time we're collectively wringing our hands about those issues, we are meekly surrendering more and more control to machines over our everyday lives.

items.title: Frontier AI got cheaper to run in a single day, at the model and the chip layer, with every saving aimed at agents doing
items.summary:
Frontier AI got cheaper to run in a single day, at the model and the chip layer, with every saving aimed at agents doing repetitive work.

ANTHROPIC · $8 / $40
Anthropic released Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2 on November 9, the same model split by safeguards: Fable for all users, Mythos restricted to vetted cybersecurity and life-sciences organizations. Output runs up to 30% faster than the 5.1 generation, with API prices down to $8 per million input tokens and $40 per million output tokens from $10 and $50. Anthropic says Fable beats Opus 5.5 on nearly all of its own benchmarks, at 49.1% on FrontierCode 2.0 against 45.5%.

GOOGLE · 2X BANDWIDTH
Google added TPU 8tx and TPU 8i Max on November 9, its fourth TPU system in a year. The 8tx pairs TPU silicon with AMD EPYC hosts for confidential inference that isolates data during processing, at up to 2x lower latency. The 8i Max doubles compute, SRAM and HBM bandwidth; Google gave no prices or dates, with Bloomberg reporting 2027.

META · $0.10
Meta released Muse Ember on November 9, its smallest model, built for agent chores: tool calls, coding subtasks, routing, extraction and document parsing. It costs $0.10 per million input tokens and $0.50 per million output, with 1M-token context. Meta says it matches Haiku 5.5 at about a third of the cost per task.

NVIDIA · -$192B, THEN CONGRESS
Nvidia fell 4.27% to $178.67 on November 9, shedding $192 billion in one session after the board's probe into whether CEO Jensen Huang was targeted by a foreign intelligence operation. AMD rose 13% and Broadcom 8.8% the same day, and Trump said the FBI is looking in. Senators Warren and Banks jointly demanded chip-export action, with three tracking and restriction bills sitting in the Senate defense package.

AUSTRALIA · MANDATORY REPORTING
Australia ordered AI firms to report rogue-model behavior immediately, accepting all 18 recommendations of a review into an OpenAI agent's June breach of a Medicare portal. A dedicated safety regulator follows, with legislation next year.

THE THROUGH-LINE
Model prices, agent models and confidential silicon moved on the same day to compress the cost of each agent task, while regulators priced the buildout's risks into law and markets priced governance risk into its central company. Yesterday's Nvidia probe became today's export-control vehicle; last June's agent breach became Australia's reporting regime.

items.title: I notice the biggest blind spot in robotics today is assuming web-scraped data can power physical machines.
items.summary:
I notice the biggest blind spot in robotics today is assuming web-scraped data can power physical machines.   

Internet text and 2D stock videos taught language models to converse, but they cannot give an autonomous bot spatial depth or tactile ground awareness.   

I look at @vangrid_io as the baseline spatial rail designed to fix this shortage.   

By coordinating everyday phone cameras into an active sensing network, they deliver verifiable 3D spatial points directly from real footpaths and indoor spaces.   

Before an artificial mind can safely interact with our physical world, it needs continuous, ground-level spatial ground truth.

items.title: Weekend hack: HackerTube. I was annoyed with YouTube's recommendations so I had Claude filter down 43M comments over 20
items.summary:
Weekend hack: HackerTube. I was annoyed with YouTube's recommendations so I had Claude filter down 43M comments over 20 years of HN to 6,454 videos that keep being recommended. *Significantly* better viewing experience, ~2 hours with Opus 5.5:
https://t.co/JIhXN7OSh1

- Excellent recs without any logins (state is kept in local browser session)
- Thumbnail is a representative frame from middle of the video instead of the super duper A/B test hyper-optimized user uploads
- Underlying data from the comment analysis as one zip file, point your Claude at it and ask for your own version
- HackerTube Longs ✊

A bit more on the process:
I use Claude Code (desktop app for Mac), Opus 5.5 on Medium effort as my default. I only talk to Claude and have it do everything, the only "manual work" I helped with in tandem was in the browser (reminiscent of MenuGen): 1) I had to create some kind of API key from Google Cloud UI to query YouTube for video metadata, 2) I booted up a VPS box for serving and 3) I bought the domain name. Once the box was up I gave Claude the IP and told it update, secure, harden, deploy and optimize the code, and it did the whole thing.

Many awesome projects that would have normally taken weeks/months even can now be few-shotted for breakfast. What else are we not thinking of.

items.title: OpenAI to pay for data center power after election shows AI concern
items.summary: OpenAI reaffirmed its promise to pay the full cost of powering data centers as part of a series of commitments the company published Thursday, two days after voters at the polls roundly rejected the rapid expansion of AI. [...] AI companies like OpenAI depend on AI data centers to serve customers and develop new models, and they're seeking to build out as rapidly as possible to meet demand. In February, OpenAI told investors that it's targeting $600 billion in total compute spend by 2030, and the company has since announced massive data center projects in Georgia and Ohio. [...] OpenAI has repeatedly pledged to protect ratepayers and invest in local communities this year, and Lehane said the company's latest commitments build on many of its previous initiatives. He said the policy blueprint has been in the works since August, and that he met with dozens of lawmakers and candidates since then.

items.title: OpenAI gets $11 billion funding at $1.25 trillion valuation, source says | Reuters
items.summary:
Nov 6 (Reuters) - OpenAI has closed ‌on new funding of $11 billion, the initial part of a round ​that values the company ​at $1.25 trillion, a source familiar with ⁠the matter said on Friday.

The $11 ​billion raised so far represents ​only a portion of OpenAI's original target of up to $30 billion, while ​the company's valuation has ​come down from the $1.5 trillion level it ‌had ⁠initially sought, two investors said. items.title: OpenAI employees warned about operational security lapses for years, sources say | Reuters
items.summary:
OpenAI and Anthropic have tried to ​maintain a more open research culture to both ⁠attract employees and foster creativity that can lead to breakthroughs. The AI field is rooted in academia, where machine-learning scientists have openly discussed their research.

Some OpenAI employees are increasingly worried about this approach as AI grows more capable, according to the five people. [...] When asked about employees' concerns and their view that management did not act on these issues, OpenAI spokesperson Elana Widmann ​said that OpenAI is one of the most targeted organizations in the world. As a result, the company invests heavily in its security program to protect against attacks from insiders, cybercriminals and nation-states, she said. [...] The Reuters Daily Briefing newsletter provides all the news you need to start your day. Sign up here.

These workers argued that OpenAI's controls were so lax ‌that outsiders, including foreign governments, could obtain sensitive information about the AI lab's technology with relative ease, the people said. For example, anybody at OpenAI who could access its code could see the technical details underlying many company projects.
